title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part II of the notes computes S0T_{0,I} for card I = 4. This is the Teichmüller groupoid of genus 0 with 4 marked points, enriched by tangent-vector (framing) data at the marked points. Notation from the previous page: J is the 3-element set of (2,2)-partitions of I, Σ = Σ_I is the J-marked projective line, M_{0,I} ≅ Σ∖J and \hat M_{0,I} ≅ Σ. S_I acts through S_I → S_J. For α ∈ J, the point α~ = α' is the second fixed point of the transposition σ_α. The set ω(J) = ord(J) of cyclic orders (orientations) of J embeds as the two S_J^+-fixed points.

This page makes Σ_J algebraic and canonically linearised.
(1) Set V(J) = ker(O^J --sum--> O), a rank-2 S_J-equivariant free module, and Σ_J = P(V(J)) (EGA convention: points are rank-1 quotients). Since rank V = 2, P(V) ≅ P(V^∨).
(2) The marked point α* is the quotient pr_α : V(J) → O. Its kernel is locally O·(β−γ), where {β, γ} = J∖{α}.
(3) The 'antipodal' point α' (the other fixed point of σ_α, i.e. the harmonic conjugate of α* with respect to β*, γ*) is given by the vector −2α+β+γ ∈ V(J).
(4) Let Δ_{α'} be the line it spans. Then 0 → Δ_{α'} → V(J) → O_{α'}(1) → 0, where O_{α'}(1) is the fibre of O(1) at α'.
(5) pr_β : Δ_{α'} → O is an isomorphism for β ≠ α, independent of β, since pr_β(−2α+β+γ) = 1.
(6) Taking determinants: det V(J) ≅ O_{α'}(1). From the defining sequence, det V(J) ≅ det O^J ≅ O ⊗_Z Z(ω), i.e. Z twisted by the orientation (sign) torsor of J. So the fibre of O(1) at each α' is canonically O ⊗ Z(ω), S_J-equivariantly with the sign twist.
(7) Application: the tangent line bundle \hat P_i of the universal curve X_{0,I} along the section i, extended over \hat M_{0,I} = Σ_I, is isomorphic to O(1) ⊗_Z L(ω). There are only two possible equivariant twists, L(ω) = Z or L(ω) = Z(ω), each functorial in (J, i).
(8) Settling the alternative is deferred to the next page. There Grothendieck restricts to the points α' and compares with a degeneration attached to a 'square structure' on I. He finds L = Z, so \hat T_i ≅ O(1). Hence the product of the tangent G_m-torsors is V*(O(1)) ∧_{G_m} G_m^I. Its π_1 over Σ* (C² minus three lines through 0, whose π_1 is P_3 ≅ F_2 × Z) yields S T_{0,4} ≅ π_1(V*(O(1))|Σ*) ∧_Z Z^I.

Purpose: an explicit, canonically S_I-equivariant model of the genus-0, 4-point tangentially-framed Teichmüller groupoid. This is the basic 'brick' of the tower in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error detected in the determinant computation: det V ≅ Δ ⊗ (V/Δ), and det of ker(sum) is the sign-twisted trivial bundle.

Minor: the identification P(V) ≅ P̌(V) is canonical only as schemes; the O(1)'s differ by the twist det V = O ⊗ Z(ω). This is exactly the sign ambiguity the page then has to resolve, so it is a subtlety rather than an error.

Degree sanity check: psi-classes on M̄_{0,4} have degree 1, so the tangent line has degree −1 in the classical sense. This is consistent with EGA conventions only if the V(O(1)) of the next page is read as the line bundle whose sheaf of sections is O(−1). This is plausible, given that V*(O(1)) is then C² minus 0, but not verifiable from this page alone.

ideas.what: Model of M̄_{0,4} as P(V(J)), V(J) = ker(sum: O^J → O), J = the 3 pair-partitions of I; marked points pr_α; harmonic conjugates as the vectors −2α+β+γ
ideas.modern_name: S_3-equivariant (reduced standard representation) model of M̄_{0,4} ≅ P^1 with cross-ratio boundary points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and its S_4 symmetry, but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Fibre of O(1) at the S_J^+-fixed / antipodal points is canonically Z twisted by the orientation torsor of J (det of the reduced permutation representation)
ideas.modern_name: sign-character twist of the equivariant linearisation; orientation torsor

ideas.what: Determining the S_I-equivariant isomorphism type of the tangent (psi) line bundle at a marked point on M̄_{0,4}, up to the sign twist L(ω)
ideas.modern_name: equivariant psi-class / cotangent line bundle on M̄_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in moduli theory (Mumford, Kontsevich, etc.)

ideas.what: Teichmüller groupoid with tangent-vector data at marked points as π_1 of a product of punctured tangent torsors (finished on the next page: C² minus three lines, i.e. pure braid group P_3 ⊗ Z^I)
ideas.modern_name: framed / tangential-base-point Teichmüller groupoid; framed mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov (tangential base points / framed groupoid)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to Teichmüller groupoids with tangential data but gives no computation

missed.claim: A careful canonical (S_I-equivariant, including the sign twist by the orientation torsor of J) description of the tangent-line torsors on M̄_{0,4}. This leads on the next page to an explicit model of the framed Teichmüller groupoid S T_{0,4} as π_1(C² minus 3 lines) ∧_Z Z^I. Later literature uses framed/tangential versions but rarely tracks this sign-linearisation subtlety explicitly.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Precise equivariant normalisation matters for Galois/GT-actions on framed braid groupoids. A sign mistake changes the extension class of the Z^I-central part. Mainly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck working out the framed tower explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially routine computation (determinant of the reduced permutation representation, equivariant linearisation of O(1) on M̄_{0,4}). The framed Teichmüller groupoid it serves is now standard via tangential base points and framed mapping class groups. Historically interesting as an explicit unpublished worked case, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'V(J) défini par une [?]' is likely 'défini par la suite exacte' (the exact sequence follows).

Margin insertion '𝓛 Sei usuel des 𝔛_{0,I} sur M_{0,I} le long de la section i ∈ I' is likely 'le fibré tangent usuel des X_{0,I} sur M_{0,I} le long de la section i ∈ I'; the next page explicitly says 'fibré tangent le long de la section i'.
'Quant à α'' refers to α~ (the antipodal fixed point of σ_α from the previous page), not a new object.
'⊗_Z Z(ω)' annotation reads 'Z tordu par ω ∈ ord(J)', i.e. Z twisted by the cyclic-order (orientation) torsor.
'(une [?]) l'alternative' is probably 'où, une seule des deux, l'alternative' or similar: one of two alternatives for L(ω).
